title: Tech Note: Creating a Ribbon-Style Toolbar in 4D
author: Timothy Aaron Penner, Technical Services Engineer, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: Design Mode project forms for toolbar pages

historical_commentary.text: Building a Microsoft-Office-style ribbon toolbar from a subform container whose source form is swapped via OBJECT SET SUBFORM is a classic-language UI trick that still works in current 4D versions, since subforms and this command remain part of the platform. The technique itself is dated in the sense that it requires manually crafting multiple pixel-matched project forms and toggling line visibility to fake a connected-tab look, a level of manual craftsmanship that later 4D UI features (and, more broadly, modern web-based/HTML-form UI) can reduce. As a classic Design Mode UI recipe, it remains functional and directly applicable to today's forms, whether stored in binary structures or Project Mode's text-based .4DForm files.
related_updates: Project Mode (4D v17+, 2018) changed the on-disk format of forms to JSON but the subform/OBJECT SET SUBFORM technique itself is unaffected
For richer navigation UI, developers today may also consider building tabbed/ribbon-like interfaces using HTML/CSS forms (4D v18+) instead of the classic manual subform-swap approach
